title: Apsis — looking for feedback on my browser survival/horror demo, try it now!
author: Zenpher
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I shared **Apsis** yesterday, but the post didn’t get much traction. Someone chickened out during a playthrough on Discord (which I’m choosing to count as positive feedback). I could use a slightly larger sample size though 😅

It’s a first-person survival/horror game that runs entirely in your browser, and I’d love some early feedback on the demo I've put together.

**You can play it here:** https://apsis.formandelement.com/  
*A dedicated GPU or Apple Silicon is recommended.*

**The premise:**

> It’s 1979. You wake up inside a crashed ship near the Russian–Chinese border. Mysterious beings are hunting you.

I’m particularly interested in:

- **Performance and bugs:** How does it run on your setup? Did anything break or behave strangely?
- **Atmosphere:** Did anything genuinely scare you? Where did the tension fall flat?
- **Gameplay:** What felt engaging, confusing, or frustrating? What felt missing?
- **Controller support:** How does it feel? There’s support for adaptive triggers and haptic feedback with a **wired DualSense**, so I’d especially appreciate feedback from anyone trying that.

This is still an early, fairly linear demo for testing ideas, with plenty of mechanics yet to come. I’m also testing a multiplayer survival build, but right now I’d really like to know whether this demo gets the basics right.

Even a couple of sentences about why you chose to not try it out would help a lot.

Thanks for giving it a go :)

comments.author: MyTech_Vibes
comments.body: It looks awesome. I too, would chicken out

comments.author: thelonelyemptiness
comments.body:
Hi!

I've just played it a bit, it looks really interesting. I've felt some outer wilds vibe on it, the atmosphere, scenario and style. Maybe it would be nice to have a narrative like, maybe some dialogues or text boxes, an intro, and these dialogues could be even just text without dubbing, but with sfx. I've even got a jumpscare on the office area when I went out xD  
About performance, I think its the main point to take a look. It feels very heavy and laggy, but I think this happens with almost any game that runs on browser, maybe adapting it to a game engine or somehow making it as a desktop app could make it use better pc resources.  
On gameplay, I can say the flashlight its a bit too much bright, even more inside buildings.  
I played on keyboard and mouse and its ok.   
I also think it would be nice to have advanced graphics options, so it would be possible to tweak and get more performance and also a manual save option.

replies.author: Zenpher
replies.body:
Thank you so much, yup performance is a real issue. Yesterday I got some feedback around waypoints, navigation, controls and loading times which were all added just before I reposted. So very much still a work in progress.

Did you pick up the ringing pager at the start? That's currently what I have to drive the narrative along with various eyewitness reports you can pick up and read scattered around the game world. I'm going to play around with dialogue next and see what I can do.

replies.author: thelonelyemptiness
replies.body: Yes, I've picked it up and its a interesting concept, but I think it felt more like focused on quests
